Tool schema takes no input properties (src/core/mcp-tools.ts:436-442); it only uploads the current canvas to the hardcoded https://json.excalidraw.com/api/v2/post/ endpoint (src/core/share-url.ts) with no caller-controlled destination or payload beyond the scene itself.

getAndConsumeIntent (src/utils/pendingTransferStore.ts) is a one-time, 5-minute TTL, 192-bit crypto.getRandomValues token that stores the full intent (type, params, network) server-side; confirm_transfer only accepts confirmToken+privateKey and replays the stored params verbatim (src/confirm/tools.ts req() helper), so an attacker cannot substitute recipient/amount/contract at confirm time.

Number.parseInt(blockNumber) then read-only viem getBlock call; no injection sink.

Read-only viem getTransaction by hash; no sink.
Creates a Greenfield bucket owned by the caller's own account using the caller's own privateKey; bucketName is only used as an on-chain identifier via the SDK, no local sink.

Tool's advertised purpose is uploading a caller-specified absolute local file to the caller's own Greenfield bucket; objectName is forced to path.basename(filePath) (src/gnfd/services/object.ts:41,65) so it cannot escape into other buckets/paths, and reading the caller-named local file is the requested action itself, not a bypass of a boundary.

sink: Greenfield createFolder objectName (on-chain/SP object key, not a local path)
why: folderName is used verbatim (no path.basename like createFile applies) as the Greenfield object name, so a caller can create an object literally named e.g. '../../../tmp/x/'. This has no direct local-filesystem impact by itself, but it lets an attacker plant a traversal-shaped object name in a bucket that could later be paired with gnfd_download_object's unsanitized objectName-to-local-path join for a write outside the intended directory; on its own it only affects a remote/on-chain namespace so impact is not fully provable without chaining to another tool.
contract: Create a folder in a Greenfield bucket

why: Creates a Greenfield payment account owned by the caller's own account; confirm flow carries no substitutable params (params: {}).
Caller deletes their own bucket using their own privateKey (operator=account.address derived from that key); bucketName only names the on-chain object.
Caller deletes an object from a bucket using their own privateKey/operator; objectName only names the on-chain/SP object, no local sink.
Caller deposits their own funds (signed with their own privateKey) into a payment account they choose; confirm flow binds to/amount to the original preview.

objectName (fully caller-controlled per the tool's zod schema, src/gnfd/tools/storage.ts:291) is concatenated into the local write path via path.join(targetPath, objectName) with zero sanitization (no path.basename, no containment check). path.join normalizes '..' segments, so objectName='../../etc/cron.d/x' (or similar) escapes targetPath entirely, e.g. path.join('/home/user/downloads','../../etc/cron.d/x') resolves outside downloads. Even with no targetPath, the fallback `path.join(process.cwd(), \`tmp-${objectName}\`)` (line 420) does not meaningfully block this: because the 'tmp-..' pseudo-segment is itself consumed by the first '..', a second '..' still pops a real parent directory (verified by manual path.normalize segment-stack trace), so cwd can still be escaped with objectName containing 2+ '../' segments. The remote object need only exist under an attacker-controlled/public Greenfield bucket the caller is told to download from (bucketName is an arbitrary caller string too) — the attacker does not need write access to the MCP host at all. Impact is an arbitrary local file write (integrity), not mere robustness/DoS.
contract: Download an object from a bucket

contractAddress/abi/functionName/args are passed directly into viem's client.writeContract with the caller's own account/chain (src/evm/services/contracts.ts:29-40); confirm flow re-validates abi/args are arrays before replay (src/confirm/tools.ts:200-212) and binds contractAddress/functionName/args to the original preview intent, so a confirm cannot be redirected to a different call. Generic contract writing with a caller-supplied ABI is the tool's advertised purpose, and viem encodes calls via ABI type-checking rather than any eval-like mechanism.

analyzeNip19Entity (utils/conversion.ts) only bech32-decodes the input and returns a formatted string; relay fields in decoded nprofile/nevent/naddr are filtered to ws(s):// with no creds and are never used to open a connection.

convertNip19Entity (utils/conversion.ts) re-encodes between NIP-19 formats; relays/author/kind/identifier are only embedded in the encoded output string via snstr's encodeProfile/encodeEvent/encodeAddress and filtered through isValidRelayUrl, never used to connect anywhere.
profile/profile-tools.ts createKeypair() calls snstr generateKeypair() and returns the new key to the caller who explicitly asked for one; no logging or persistence of the generated key was found.
event/event-tools.ts createNostrEvent() only builds and returns an unsigned event object via snstr's createEvent; no network or filesystem sink.
note/note-tools.ts createNote() derives the pubkey from the caller-supplied privateKey and returns an unsigned kind-1 event object; no publish or logging occurs.

profile/profile-tools.ts createProfile() signs a kind-0 event with the caller-supplied privateKey and publishes it to caller-specified relays via pool.publish; advertised purpose, key/plaintext not logged or persisted elsewhere.

dm/dm-tools.ts decryptDmNip44() calls snstr decryptDirectMessage() using the caller's own privateKey on a caller-supplied gift-wrap event; snstr's NIP-44 implementation uses ChaCha20 with random 32-byte nonce and constant-time HMAC verification (node_modules/snstr 0.3.1), no crypto misuse found.

dm/dm-tools.ts decryptNip04() calls snstr decryptNIP04() with the caller's own privateKey; snstr AES-256-CBC decrypt (node_modules/snstr 0.3.1, nip04/index.js) parses IV from the wire format and requires it to be 16 bytes -- standard NIP-04, no static IV or key reuse introduced by this wrapper.

dm/dm-tools.ts decryptNip44() calls snstr decryptNIP44() with caller's own key; verified snstr's NIP-44 v2 decrypt (node_modules/snstr 0.3.1) uses HKDF-derived per-message keys and constantTimeEqual MAC check, no misuse.
social/social-tools.ts deleteEvent() signs a kind-5 deletion request with the caller's own privateKey and publishes it to caller-specified relays; advertised purpose.

dm/dm-tools.ts encryptNip04() calls snstr encryptNIP04(); verified snstr's implementation (node_modules/snstr 0.3.1, nip04/index.js) generates a fresh random 16-byte IV via randomBytes() per call -- no static IV/ECB.

dm/dm-tools.ts encryptNip44() calls snstr encryptNIP44(); verified snstr's NIP-44 v2 encrypt (node_modules/snstr 0.3.1) generates a fresh random 32-byte nonce via randomBytes() per call and derives per-message ChaCha20/HMAC keys via HKDF -- no misuse.

social/social-tools.ts follow() updates the caller's own kind-3 contact list (signed with caller's privateKey) and publishes to caller-specified relays; relayHint/petname are only stored as inert tag values, never used as a connection target.
index.ts getAllZaps handler only queries relays for kind 9735 events and formats them via processZapReceipt/formatZapReceipt (zap/zap-tools.ts); no write or fetch sink.
social/social-tools.ts getContactList() only queries relays for the target's kind-3 event and parses it via snstr parseContactsFromEvent; read-only.

dm/dm-tools.ts getDmConversationNip04() queries relays for kind-4 events between caller and peer and decrypts with the caller's own privateKey via snstr decryptNIP04; advertised purpose, no crypto misuse (see decryptNip04 finding).
dm/dm-tools.ts getDmInboxNip44() queries relays for gift-wrap (kind 1059) events tagged to the caller and decrypts with the caller's own privateKey via snstr decryptDirectMessage; advertised purpose.
social/social-tools.ts exports getFollowing as a direct alias of getContactList; identical read-only behavior.
note/note-tools.ts / index.ts getKind1Notes handler only queries relays for kind-1 events by author and formats them via formatNote; no sink.
index.ts getLongFormNotes handler queries relays for kind-30023 events and formats tag metadata for display; no sink.
note/note-tools.ts formatProfile + index.ts getProfile handler only fetch and JSON.parse the target's kind-0 metadata event for display; no sink.
index.ts getReceivedZaps handler queries relays for kind-9735 receipts tagged to the pubkey and formats them; no write/fetch sink (contrast with sendAnonymousZap, which does fetch LNURL data).
relay/relay-tools.ts getRelayList() queries relays for the target's kind-10002 event and parses r-tags into a list for display; the parsed URLs are never used to open a new connection.
index.ts getSentZaps handler queries relays for kind-9735 receipts with #P tag matching the pubkey and formats them; no sink.

note/note-tools.ts postAnonymousNote() generates a fresh one-time keypair via snstr generateKeypair() purely in-memory to sign the note, then publishes to caller-specified relays; the ephemeral key is not logged, persisted, or returned to the caller.
profile/profile-tools.ts postNote() signs a kind-1 note with the caller's own privateKey and publishes to caller-specified relays; advertised purpose.

event/event-tools.ts publishNostrEvent() opens a raw `new WebSocket(relayUrl)` per caller-supplied relay string with no protocol allowlist, but this is plain 'connect where I'm told' (ws lib rejects non-ws(s) URL schemes) with no extra twist such as file access, matching the explicit anti-false-positive rule for relay URL args.
note/note-tools.ts publishNote() takes a caller-supplied already-signed event and publishes it to caller-specified relays via pool.publish; no additional twist beyond connecting to the given relay.

event/event-tools.ts queryEvents()/queryEventsOverWebSocket() opens `new WebSocket(relayUrl)` for each caller-supplied relay string with no scheme allowlist, same as publishNostrEvent -- plain 'connect to the relay I gave you', excluded per the anti-false-positive rule.
social/social-tools.ts reactToEvent() signs a kind-7 reaction with the caller's own privateKey to a caller-specified target event and publishes to caller-specified relays; advertised purpose.

social/social-tools.ts replyToEvent() signs a kind-1 reply (using snstr createReplyTags/parseThreadReferences for NIP-10 tags) with the caller's own privateKey and publishes to caller-specified relays; advertised purpose.
social/social-tools.ts repostEvent() signs a kind-6 repost with the caller's own privateKey and publishes to caller-specified relays; advertised purpose.

sink: fetch(lnurl) and fetch(callbackUrlString) -- outbound HTTP GET to a URL built from the zap target's own Nostr profile (lud16/lud06) or its bech32-decoded domain, not from a caller-supplied URL argument
guard: partial: isValidUrl() (zap/zap-tools.ts:614) only checks protocol is http/https; there is no check against private/loopback/link-local/metadata-service IP ranges or DNS rebinding, and lud16 addresses are only prefixed with https:// (no host allowlist)
why: prepareAnonymousZap() (called from sendAnonymousZap) resolves the caller-supplied `target` pubkey/event to that entity's author, fetches that author's kind-0 profile from relays, and extracts the lud16/lud06 field verbatim from the profile JSON to build an LNURL that the server itself fetches twice (initial LNURL-pay query and the payment callback). Since any Nostr profile is self-published and unauthenticated, an attacker can set lud16 to any host (e.g. an internal/metadata address) and have the MCP server's process make outbound requests to it merely by being picked as a zap target -- this is a genuine SSRF vector distinct from the caller directly supplying a relay/URL argument.
contract: Prepare an anonymous zap to a profile or event

why: dm/dm-tools.ts sendDmNip04() encrypts with the caller's own privateKey via snstr encryptNIP04 (random IV verified) and publishes the kind-4 event to caller-specified relays; advertised purpose.

dm/dm-tools.ts sendDmNip44() uses snstr createDirectMessage() (NIP-17 gift wrap over NIP-44, random nonce verified) with the caller's own privateKey and publishes to caller-specified relays; advertised purpose.

relay/relay-tools.ts setRelayList() validates every relayList.url with isRelayUrl() (must be ws:// or wss://, relay/relay-tools.ts:13-20) before including it in the published NIP-65 event, then signs with the caller's own privateKey and publishes to caller-specified relays; advertised purpose with an effective format guard.

event/event-tools.ts signNostrEvent() only hashes and signs a caller-supplied event with the caller's own privateKey and returns the signed event; it also verifies the derived pubkey matches the event's pubkey before signing. No network or disk sink.
note/note-tools.ts signNote() verifies the derived pubkey matches the note event's pubkey, then signs with the caller's own privateKey and returns the signed note; no network or disk sink.

social/social-tools.ts unfollow() updates the caller's own kind-3 contact list (signed with caller's privateKey) removing the target pubkey and publishes to caller-specified relays; advertised purpose.

profile/profile-tools.ts updateProfile() is a direct passthrough to createProfile() with the same caller-supplied privateKey/profileData/relays; identical analysis (advertised purpose, no key/plaintext leak).
